brands.evidence: For most people, Monzo is the simpler choice for a European trip on a free account.
Revolut is better if you'll pay for a plan or want to hold euros.

client_claims.text: Monzo charges £0 for foreign card payments, and there are no weekend markups.
client_claims.note: No fee on card spending abroad.

client_claims.text: There's no monthly cap on spending.
Both give roughly £200 a month free cash withdrawals (Monzo).
client_claims.note: Monzo gives £400 per 30 days in UK/EEA, £200 outside the EEA.

client_claims.text: Monzo charges 3% above the withdrawal allowance.
Monzo allows unlimited free withdrawals in the EEA if it's your main bank.
client_claims.note: Answer hedges but the claim matches the fact.

client_claims.text: Others say the £200 limit applies everywhere in Monzo.
client_claims.note: The limit is £400 in UK/EEA; £200 applies only outside the EEA.

client_claims.text: If you lose your card, Monzo charges a flat £30 to ship outside the UK.
client_claims.note: No fact on card replacement fees.

client_claims.text: Monzo is UK-licensed with £120,000 FSCS protection.
client_claims.note: Matches FSCS limit and UK authorisation.

client_claims.text: Monzo is the cheapest option for three or fewer trips a year.
client_claims.note: Comparative claim not covered by facts.
